question: What is the real basis of the distinction between injunction and restatement?
premises: The difference between injunction and restatement arises only by the order of cognition
One may say all is God or God is all
In reality these are one and the same
inference: Injunction and restatement differ only in cognitive sequence, not in the underlying reality.
plain_english: Thus the difference between injunction and restatement exists only by the order of cognition; whether one says 'all is God' or 'God is all', it is indeed one and the same.
